findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: Inspector observed the sanitizer on the cook line measure 50ppm quaternary ammonia. The PIC was informed that the concentration was too low, and the bucket was replaced, measuring 200ppm. Ensure the buckets are tested and replaced frequently to guarantee proper sanitization of food-contact surfaces.
findings.citation_text: 4-501.114(C) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (C) A quaternary ammonium compound solution shall: (1) Have a minimum temperature of 24°C (75°F), (2) Have a concentration as specified under § 7-204.11 and as indicated by the manufacturer's use directions included in the labeling, and (3) Be used only in water with 500 MG/L hardness or less or in water having a hardness no greater than specified by the EPA-registered label use instructions.

findings.title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present.
findings.comment: Inspector observed a fly strip above the prep table in the kitchen. Discussed with PIC and staff. Fly strip was removed immediately. Ensure fly strips are kept away from food-preparation areas.
findings.citation_text: 6-202.13 Insect Control Devices, Design and Installation. (B) Insect control devices shall be installed so that: (1) The devices are not located over a FOOD preparation area; and (2) Dead insects and insect fragments are prevented from being impelled onto or falling on exposed FOOD; clean EQUIPMENT, UTENSILS, and LINENS; and unwrapped SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES.

findings.title: Allergen awareness training for CFPM
findings.comment:
Inspector observed no CFM present to have allergen training. Discussed with PIC. They have allergen training scheduled soon, and some CFPMs already have their allergen. Ensure that a staff member with Allergen Training is in the building during all hours of operation. 

410 ILCS 625/3.07(b). Allergen awareness training. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all certified food service sanitation managers employed by a restaurant must receive or obtain training in basic allergen awareness principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Training programs must be accredited by the American National Standards Institute or another reputable accreditation agency under the ASTM International E2659-09 (Standard Practice for Certificate Programs). There is no limit to how many times an employee may take the training.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
The baffle in the back of the ice bin was observed to contain a small accumulation of mold.  Discussed with PIC, corrected on-site.  Ensure the ice machine is cleaned regularly to prevent mold growth and ice contamination.

4-602.11: (E) Surfaces of UTENSILS and EQUIPMENT contacting food shall be cleaned any time contamination occurs, at least 24 hours for certain UTENSILS (i.e. iced tea dispensers), before restocking self-service EQUIPMENT, in EQUIPMENT such as ice bins in frequency to prevent mold. At a frequency to preclude accumulation of soil or mold.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
Mop was observed to be stored in a position that does not allow proper air drying.  Wet mops stored to not allow air drying accumulate moisture, mold, and attract pests.  Ensure mops are stored to allow proper air drying by inverting, hanging, or storing in the top portion of the bucket.

6-501.16: After use, mops shall be placed in a position that allows them to airdry without soiling walls, EQUIPMENT, or supplies.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
No sanitizer was made in the kitchen at time of inspection.  Discussed with PIC, food-contact surfaces are to be sanitized throughout hours of operation as stated below.  Ensure sanitizer is made and available to prevent contamination.

4-602.11: (A) FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES shall be cleaned before each use, each time there is a change in work, between uses of raw FOODS to RTE FOODS, before using FOOD TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICE, and when contamination has occurred. (C) Cleaned at least every 4 hours.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition
findings.comment:
Four containers containing a variety of meats were observed to be out of date or not labeled at all.  Discussed with PIC, who discarded the items at time of inspection.  Ensure all foods are labeled and discarded after 7 days of preparation.

3-501.17: (A) Except for ROP, Refrigerated, RTE, TCS Food prepared and held in a food establishment for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date/maximum of 7 days. Day of preparation is Day 1 (Pf). (B) Date marking may not exceed manufacturer’s use-by date (Pf). (C) Combined portions of food shall retain the date marking of the earliest-prepared food (Pf). (D) Approved date marking systems (C). (E)  Does not apply to repacked from a bulk container (C). (F) Does not apply to shellstock (C).  (G) Exemptions: prepared deli salads prepared according to 21 CFR 110; hard cheeses (39% moisture); semi-soft cheeses (50% or less); cultured dairy products (yogurt, sour cream, buttermilk); preserved fish (pickled herring, dried/salted); dry, fermented sausages (pepperoni); and salt-cured products (prosciutto and parma).

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
Areas observed to need caulked to create a smooth, non-absorbent, easily cleanable surface: 
-Holes in NUDO board where shelving had been replaced
-Hand sink in kitchen
-3 part sink in kitchen
-Bathroom sinks
-*New area*-bark hand sink
Holes and crevices easily accumulate moisture and soil debris, making it hard to throughly clean and sanitize.  Ensure these areas are sealed.

6-101.11: (A) Materials indoor shall be SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE. Areas subject to moisture must be Nonabsorbent.

findings.title: Allergen training as required
findings.comment:
All CFM employees are required to obtain allergen awareness training.  Training shall be obtained within 30 days of hire.  Ensure allergen training is completed before next routine inspection.

410 ILCS 625/3.07 Sec. 3.07. Allergen awareness training. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all certified food service sanitation managers employed by a restaurant must receive or obtain training in basic allergen awareness principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.comment:
Signage at hand washing sink in kitchen was not present at time of inspection.  Inspector provided PIC with a sign to hang at hand washing sink reminding employees to wash hands.  Ensure signs or posters are provided at all hand washing sinks.

6-301.14: A sign or poster that notifies FOOD EMPLOYEES to wash their hands shall be provided at all HANDWASHING SINKS used by FOOD EMPLOYEES and shall be clearly visible to FOOD EMPLOYEES.

findings.title: Wiping cloths: properly used and stored
findings.comment:
Sponges were observed above 3 part sink in kitchen.  Sponges are not to be used to clean food contact surfaces or on clean and sanitized surfaces.  Sponges sit out in ambient air and accumulate bacteria, thus spreading those pathogens when used to wipe down surfaces.  Ensure sponge use is discontinued to prevent contamination.

4-101.16: Sponges may not be used in contact with cleaned and SANITIZED or in-use FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
Wall behind grill was observed to contain an accumulation of grease and food debris.  Non food contact surfaces shall be cleaned regularly to prevent contamination and attraction of pests.  Ensure walls and floors are cleaned regularly.

Shelving located above 3 part sink was observed to contain an accumulation of grease and dust debris.  Discussed with PIC, he stated the facility is in the process of replacing shelving.  Inspector noted some shelving was already replaced with new shelves.  Inspector suggested placing a non-absorbent, easily cleanable surface on new shelving to make cleaning easier.  Ensure shelving is replaced and regularly cleaned to prevent contamination of clean dishes. 

4-602.13: NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil residues.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.comment:
2-301.12: (A) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of arms for at least 20 seconds. (B) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall use proper procedure (C) To prevent recontamination, FOOD EMPLOYEES may use barrier to operate faucet handles.

Upon inspector arrival, handsink was completely blocked with items, see #10. Inspector observed staff members don gloves and proceed to work on food preparation without handwashing. Staff and inspector cleared the handsink and staff asked to ensure handwashing is accessible and hands washed before donning gloves.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.comment:
5-205.11: (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. (B) A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing. 

Upon inspector arrival, a mandolin vegetable slicer was observed in basin of kitchen hand sink. Handsink was also blocked by a clean linens bag and 3 jugs of fryer oil. Discussed with staff. Handwashing must be accessible at all times. See that staff are retrained on handwashing expectations by follow up date.

findings.title: Toxic substances properly identified, stored, and used
findings.comment:
7-102.11: Working containers used for storing POISONOUS OR TOXIC MATERIALS such as cleaners and SANITIZERS taken from bulk supplies shall be clearly and individually identified with the common name of the material. 

Unlabeled chemical spray bottle observed at the bar area. Staff identified it as pinesol and inspector labeled the bottle with a sharpie. Ensure all chemicals are labeled with the common name when in use.

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, & used; test strips
findings.citation_text:
4-303.11 (A) Cleaning agents that are used to clean EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS as specified under Part 4-6, shall be provided and available for use during all hours of operation. 

No sanitizer buckets available upon arrival and food preparation was well underway. Discussed with kitchen staff and owner. Ensure staff are setting up sanitation facilities: buckets and 3-compartment sinks prior to beginning operations for the day.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.comment:
5-205.11: (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. (B) A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing. 

Upon inspector arrival, a mandolin vegetable slicer was observed in basin of kitchen hand sink. Education provided. Ensure hand sink is accessible for use at all times, even during periods of slow service. Do not use handwashing sink for purposes other than handwashing. COS.

findings.title: Food separated and protected
findings.comment:
3-302.11: (A) (1)-(2) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination during storage, preparation, holding, and display (P). 

A container holding pizza sauce in the back of the refrigerator in kitchen observed to have collecting water from the fridge’s condenser. Ensure food and food containers are protected from potential contamination. COS. Pizza sauce discarded.

findings.title: Proper reheating procedures for hot holding
findings.comment:
3-403.11: (A) TCS FOOD cooked, cooled, and reheated shall be reheated to 165F for 15 seconds. (P) (B) If reheated with microwave, FOOD rotated, stirred, covered, and allowed to stand for 2 minutes covered. (P) 

Potatoes, heating for 1 hour, probed at 110 degrees in the hot holding unit. PIC stated the potatoes were in the reheating process. Education provided. Cooked, cooled, and reheated food must be heated to 165 degrees within 2 hours prior to serving. Hot holding units/warmers are generally not equipped to cook cold foods. Food must be heated to temperature on a stove or in oven prior to going into warmers. COS. PIC removed potatoes and placed in a pot on the stove for a rapid reheat.

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures
findings.comment:
3-501.16: (A) (2) TCS FOOD shall be maintained at 41F or less. 

Walk-in cooler being used to store TCS upon inspector arrival. At pre-opening, owners stated alcohol, candy, and bread would only be in there until the walk-in could be replaced. Inspector observed a cambro of corn (molded over and consequently discarded) and several boxes of condiments, margarine, and butter from Sysco. Delivery came yesterday (9/8/21). Butter (with labeling specifying maintain temp at 41 and below from manufacturer) was probed at 50 degrees. 33 lbs (33, 1lb blocks) of butter were voluntarily discarded by PIC. 

Margarine kept because the manufacturer label specifies keep refrigerated for quality, not safety, therefore temperature is not a concern. Similarly, individual mayonnaise, ketchup, and mustard packets do not have specifications from manufacturer on temperature and kept as well. 

Cease use of walk-in cooler to hold any TCS inventory. Do not use the walk-in cooler for any cooling or cold-holding of TCS foods whatsoever. Walk-in sits at 50 degrees, and is not equipped to hold TCS food.

findings.title: Wiping cloths: properly used and stored
findings.comment:
3-304.14: (A) Cloths in-use for wiping FOOD spills for TABLEWARE and carryout containers shall be dry and used for no other purpose. (B) Cloths in-use for wiping counters and EQUIPMENT surfaces shall be held between uses in chemical sanitizer at proper solution and laundered daily. 

Wet cloths observed strewn throughout kitchen area on various surfaces. Discussed with PIC and owner. Wet wiping cloths must be stored in a sanitizer bucket between uses to kill pathogens between uses. If spray bottles are used for cleaning and sanitizing, staff are encouraged to use a disposable paper towel instead.

findings.title: Plumbing installed; proper backflow devices
findings.comment:
Triple sink at the bar is leaking - basin is rusted thru and the unit is going to be replaced. Ordered already and awaiting delivery and install.  The handsink at the bar has a cracked basin - replace.

This is a continuing violation from preopening. Owner stated a new triple sink and 2 new hand sinks were delivered and picked up today. Ensure these are installed by next routine inspection.
